title: There is a name in the New Testament that almost no one preaches about.
paragraphs: There is a name in the New Testament that almost no one preaches about.
Demas.
He appears quietly in the letters of Paul.
At first, his name is listed among faithful workers.
Imagine that.
Demas once stood beside Paul during the most explosive expansion of the early church.

He witnessed miracles.
He heard the gospel preached with power.
He saw the cost of following Christ.
He wasn't on the outside looking in.
He was in the middle of it.
But by the time Paul writes his final letter, something heartbreaking appears in the text:
"Demas has deserted me, because he loved this present world." (2 Timothy 4:10)
The Bible doesn't say Demas stopped believing.
It says something more dangerous.
He loved the present world.
And that sentence reveals a powerful spiritual truth:
People rarely walk away from God because of one dramatic moment.
Most walk away because their loves slowly change.
The world begins to feel safer than sacrifice.
Comfort begins to feel better than calling.
Temporary things begin to feel more important than eternal ones.
Little by little, the heart drifts.
Until one day, the direction has completely changed.
Demas reminds us of something sobering:

You can work in ministry…
serve alongside faithful leaders…
and still allow the world to capture your heart.
Proximity to spiritual things is not the same as devotion to Christ.
And here is the question Demas leaves every believer with:
What are you slowly learning to love more?
Because the battle for faith is not just about what we believe.
It is about what we treasure.
And whatever the heart treasures most will eventually determine the path we take.
What do you think is the most common way believers today slowly drift toward loving the world more than God?
